title: Lyme Nephritis
desc: Doxycycline, an ACE inhibitor or ARB, mycophenolate, anti-thrombotic aspirin, fish oils and a renal diet — with Dr Goldstein's preference for pulse dexamethasone if steroids are needed.

meds.name: Doxycycline
meds.note: 5 mg/kg PO q 12 h. Other antibiotic choices are amoxicillin, or Convenia given as two doses two weeks apart.

meds.name: Telmisartan
meds.note: 1 mg/kg SID, to a maximum of 2 mg/kg SID.

meds.name: Losartan
meds.note: Start at 0.5 mg/kg and increase up to 1 mg/kg BID if needed.

meds.name: Prednisone
meds.desc: only if the dog is not eating
meds.note: Immunosuppressive doses, used if the dog is not eating. Dr Goldstein recommends PULSE DEXAMETHASONE rather than oral prednisone where steroids are needed.

meds.name: Baby aspirin
meds.desc: protein-losing nephropathy carries a clotting risk
meds.doseText: ¼ of a baby aspirin tablet
meds.note: Clopidogrel (Plavix) is raised on the source sheet as a possible alternative.

meds.name: Fish oils (EPA + DHA)
meds.note: 35 mg/kg/day of combined EPA + DHA — roughly 180 mg of omega-3 (EPA plus DHA) per 10 lb per day.

notes.Antibiotic options: Doxycycline 5 mg/kg BID is first choice. Other options are amoxicillin, or Convenia given as two doses two weeks apart.
notes.Steroids: If the dog is not eating, immunosuppressive doses of prednisone. Dr Goldstein recommends pulse dexamethasone rather than oral prednisone where steroids are needed.
notes.Blocking the RAAS: Either an ACE inhibitor (benazepril) or an ARB (telmisartan, irbesartan, losartan). Telmisartan 1 mg/kg SID, maximum 2 mg/kg SID.
notes.Clotting risk: Protein-losing nephropathy is prothrombotic — hence the low-dose aspirin, with clopidogrel raised as an alternative.
notes.Fish oil target: 35 mg/kg/day of EPA + DHA combined, which is about 180 mg of omega-3 per 10 lb per day.

dischargeBlocks.title: What Lyme nephritis is
dischargeBlocks.text:
Lyme disease has caused {name}'s immune system to damage the filters in the kidneys, so protein that should stay in the blood is being lost into the urine.

This is serious and we will be monitoring {name} closely. The medications work on several fronts at once: clearing the infection, protecting the kidneys, reducing the protein loss, and lowering the risk of a blood clot.

dischargeBlocks.title: The renal diet
dischargeBlocks.text:
The prescription diet is part of the treatment, not a suggestion.

- Feed only the diet we have recommended.
- No table scraps, and no treats or chews unless we have approved them.
- If {name} will not eat it, call us rather than switching back — there are other options and going hungry is worse.

dischargeBlocks.title: Water
dischargeBlocks.text:
Always leave fresh water available, in more than one place. Never restrict water — {name}'s kidneys need it.

Tell us if you notice a sudden increase or decrease in how much {name} is drinking.

dischargeBlocks.title: Call us if you notice
dischargeBlocks.text:
- Not eating, vomiting, or losing weight
- Swelling of the legs, belly or face
- Sudden breathlessness, or a leg that becomes cold, painful or will not bear weight
- Increasing tiredness, or drinking much more or much less than usual

The breathing and cold-leg signs suggest a blood clot and are an emergency.

dischargeBlocks.title: Ticks
dischargeBlocks.text:
Keep {name} on a reliable tick preventive year-round and check the coat after walks, particularly around the head, ears, neck and between the toes.

Removing a tick within 24 to 48 hours greatly reduces the chance of Lyme being transmitted.

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text:
{name} needs regular blood and urine tests so we can track kidney values, protein loss and blood pressure, and adjust the medication accordingly.

Please keep every appointment we book — this condition is managed by the numbers, not by how well {name} looks.
